subject: Bench readout — clarifying timeline & next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finserve.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call — bench readout attached and suggested next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from my side and the actions we agreed on during the call:

- Redwood ran the end-to-end latency/throughput bench on your sample workload (attached bench-report-20260701.pdf).
- Key short reads from the bench (500-token avg messages, concurrent sessions ~40):
  - p50: ~45 ms
  - p95: ~160 ms
  - p99: ~420 ms
  - Sustained throughput: ~220 tokens/sec per GPU of the configured instance
- Next steps we suggested:
  1) Your infra team validate traffic shape (we requested a short traffic CSV).
  2) We confirm whether Dedicated or Private will be preferred for compliance.
  3) We schedule a follow-up with Marcus (SE) to walk through kernel/quantization options if you want lower p99 targets.

Attachments: bench-report-20260701.pdf (summary + raw logs), redwood-govt-security-sheet.pdf

Would you say timing-wise this remains a Q3 priority for FinServe AI? If yes, we can schedule the technical deep-dive next week. If priorities shifted, a one-line update works — we’ll adjust our plan.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Samir Gupta <samir@finserve.ai>

Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call — bench readout attached and suggested next steps

Neha,

Thanks for the summary and for the detailed report — that was quick. A few clarifications from our side after a quick pass:

- The p99 number matches what our in-house sim produced on similar batch sizes, so that aligns.
- Can you confirm whether those numbers are with KV cache enabled for multi-call sessions? That matters for our chat flows.
- Also: do you have an approximate cost delta between the current profile and a quantized int8 profile that trades a bit of quality for lower p99?

I’ve looped in procurement for visibility; they’ll manage contracts once we lock scope. Marcus — could SE confirm the KV cache setting?

Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of ML Engineering | FinServe AI
samir@finserve.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finserve.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call — bench readout attached and suggested next steps

Thanks Samir — quick answers:

- The bench-report numbers included prefix/KV caching for multi-turn sessions (cache hit rates averaged ~72% during the run).
- For an int8 quantized profile we saw p99 improvements in the 15–30% range on the same hardware in our internal tests; CPU/GPU utilization dropped ~18% with a correspondingly lower token cost. Quality regressions depend on the model; we supply a small eval harness so you can validate prompt fidelity on your test set.

I can share a short kernel/params doc and a cost estimate; linking the drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleBench

If you want, I can run a quick targeted bench (same sample traces) with an int8 profile and return the delta numbers in 48 hours.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai

Samir — looping back to see if Marcus’s responses answered the team’s questions. Suggested concrete next steps:

- If you’re comfortable, Marcus can run the int8-targeted bench on your sample traces (48h turnaround). If not, we can send the eval harness and cost delta for you to validate offline.
- I can schedule a 30-minute deep-dive between Marcus and your infra/ML team next Tue or Wed (07/14 or 07/15) — prefer morning PT.
- If procurement wants an early view of commercial terms, I can share a draft SOW + estimated committed capacity to speed things up.

If I don’t hear back, I’ll nudge next week. Quick reply with preferred option is perfect.

Thanks,
Neha
